highlights.LEE2010: Loss of Sestrin in flies lets TOR run unchecked, causing fat/mitochondrial/muscle/heart pathology reversible by blocking TOR or activating AMPK.

Betz C.lab_name: Michael N. Hall Lab, Biozentrum, University of Basel (where these studies were done)
Betz C.role: Traced mTORC2 to a specific address inside the cell — the mitochondria-ER contact site
Betz C.sub: PhD & postdoc, Michael Hall lab, Biozentrum · research staff, vascular-biology groups, Biozentrum · now Head of Department, Directorate of Health, Ministry of Health (Luxembourg, per secondary sources)
story: Showed (BET2013) mTORC2 concentrates at mitochondria-associated ER membranes (MAM), phosphorylating tether proteins via Akt; disrupting mTORC2 broke the ER-mitochondria tether, damaging membrane potential/ATP/calcium handling. Co-authored the widely cited review (BETZ2013) arguing mTOR's subcellular address is a regulatory layer in its own right.
Long run in Hall's lab (2010–2018, incl. a 2018 Nature paper on LHPP as tumor suppressor). Moved into vascular biology, then public-health administration.

highlights.BETZ2013: Review arguing mTOR's subcellular location, not just activity, is a core regulatory layer.
highlights.BET2013: mTORC2-Akt signaling concentrates at mitochondria-ER contact sites, maintaining the tether required for normal mitochondrial function.

Delgoffe GM.lab_name: Delgoffe Lab, UPMC Hillman Cancer Center / University of Pittsburgh
Delgoffe GM.role: Discovered that mTOR kinase signaling is the master switch between effector and regulatory T-cell fate
Delgoffe GM.sub: PhD, Johns Hopkins (Jonathan D. Powell lab, 2010) · postdoc, St. Jude (Dario Vignali lab) · now Professor of Immunology, Director of Tumor Microenvironment Center, UPMC Hillman Cancer Center; Editor-in-Chief, Immunology (Wiley)
story: As PhD student with Powell (who has his own medailonek), showed (DEL2009) T cells lacking mTOR fail to differentiate into effector cells, defaulting toward Treg fate. Refined (DEL2011): mTORC1 required specifically for Th1/Th17, mTORC2 specifically for Th2 — which complex is active, not just mTOR on/off, dictates fate.

Built own program at Pitt around the idea that tumors selectively feed Tregs, not just starve killer T cells — blocking lactate export starves tumor Tregs (Nature 2021); dichloroacetate improves CAR-T persistence (Cell Metabolism 2024). Co-founded Novasenta and RemplirBio. CRI Lloyd J. Old STAR awardee.

highlights.DEL2009: T cells lacking mTOR fail to differentiate into effector cells, defaulting toward Treg fate.
highlights.DEL2011: mTORC1 and mTORC2 selectively program distinct CD4 helper T-cell lineages.

Lawrence RE.lab_name: Lawrence Lab, UCLA David Geffen School of Medicine
Lawrence RE.role: Discovered the nutrient-driven affinity switch and FLCN checkpoint that gate mTORC1 activation at the lysosome
Lawrence RE.sub: BA, Swarthmore College · PhD, UC Berkeley (Roberto Zoncu lab) · postdoc, UCSF/HHMI (Peter Walter lab) · now Assistant Professor, UCLA (since January 2025)
story: As Zoncu-lab PhD student (Zoncu has his own medailonek), showed (LAW2018) nutrients destabilize the Rag-Ragulator scaffold, requiring two simultaneous Rag-binding interfaces for mTORC1 capture — an affinity switch cancer mutations short-circuit. Solved (LAW2019) a 3.6 Å cryo-EM structure of the lysosomal folliculin (FLCN) complex, showing FLCN's RagC-GAP activity is auto-inhibited until the complex disassembles.

Moved to UCSF/HHMI studying the Integrated Stress Response (eIF2B allostery, ISRIB mechanism). Now own lab at UCLA since Jan 2025, studying stress-signaling feedback on metabolism and glial neurodegeneration.

highlights.LAW2018: Nutrients destabilize the Rag-Ragulator scaffold, requiring two engaged Rag interfaces for mTORC1 capture.
highlights.LAW2019: Cryo-EM shows FLCN's GAP activity is auto-inhibited within the intact lysosomal complex, gating mTORC1 activation.

Wang T.lab_name: Sabatini Lab, Whitehead Institute / MIT Biology (at time of both featured studies)
Wang T.role: Helped show that 4E-BP proteins are mTORC1's master translation-control switch and that CASTOR1 is its arginine sensor
Wang T.sub: Graduate & postdoctoral research, Sabatini Lab · later traced to Janelia Research Campus (HHMI), computational/quantitative scientist · most recent record (2024) co-affiliated with Allen Institute for Neural Dynamics — current status unconfirmed
story: Co-author (THO2012): ribosome profiling with Torin1 showed mTORC1 controls translation of TOP-motif mRNAs largely through 4E-BPs. Co-author (CHA2016): CASTOR1 identified as the direct arginine sensor upstream of mTORC1.

**Poznámka (viz flag výše):** Po Sabatini labu stopa vede na Janelia Research Campus (bioinformatika/zobrazování — spoluautor Cellpose, EASI-FISH, Neuropixels studie s Karel Svobodou), případně Allen Institute for Neural Dynamics od ~2023. **Nenašli jsme spojení na Columbia University** — nezaměňovat se stejnojmenným CRISPR-screening PI tam. Doporučuji ověřit před publikací.

highlights.THO2012: Co-authored the ribosome-profiling study showing 4E-BPs are mTORC1's master translational effectors.

Garcia-Martinez JM.lab_name: MRC Protein Phosphorylation Unit, University of Dundee (at time of both featured studies)
Garcia-Martinez JM.role: Discovered mTORC2 activates SGK1 and co-developed Ku-0063794, one of the first selective ATP-competitive mTOR inhibitors
Garcia-Martinez JM.sub: PhD, Universitat de Barcelona/IDIBAPS (Alberch lab, Huntington's disease) · postdoc, Alessi Lab, MRC Protein Phosphorylation Unit, Dundee · now Senior Scientist, Cancer Research, Boehringer Ingelheim RCV, Vienna (per most recent record, 2024; exact current title unconfirmed)
story: First author (GAR2008, with Dario Alessi, who has his own medailonek): mTORC2 — not mTORC1 — phosphorylates and activates SGK1, cleanly separating what each mTOR complex does. First author (GAR2009): co-developed Ku-0063794, one of the first genuinely selective ATP-competitive mTOR inhibitors blocking both complexes.

Continued at Dundee testing PI3K/mTOR inhibitors in mouse lymphoma models, then moved into industry — Boehringer Ingelheim's Vienna oncology unit, developing bispecific antibody drugs (TRAILR2 agonists) for colorectal/pancreatic cancer (2020, 2024 papers). **Kariérní mezera 2012–2020 nedohledána.**

highlights.GAR2008: mTORC2 (not mTORC1) phosphorylates and activates SGK1.
highlights.GAR2009: Co-developed Ku-0063794, a specific ATP-competitive inhibitor blocking both mTOR complexes.

Williams RL.lab_name: MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology (LMB), Cambridge
Williams RL.role: Reveals the atomic architecture that docks mTORC1 onto the lysosome
Williams RL.sub: BS, Purdue · MS, Eastern Washington Univ. · PhD, UC Riverside (1986) · Rutgers, Cornell, Boris Kidrič Institute Belgrade · Group Leader, MRC LMB, Cambridge
story: Cryo-EM shows TOR dimerizes through an N-terminal helical solenoid (BAR2016), shaping how mTORC1 is built. Three years later, solved mTORC1 bound to Rag GTPases (ANA2019), showing how amino-acid status recruits the complex to the lysosome.
Leads a structural biology group at the storied MRC LMB, working across the PI3K superfamily. FRS (2017), FMedSci, EMBO Member, Biochemical Society Morton Lectureship.

highlights.BAR2016: Cryo-EM shows TOR dimerizes through an N-terminal helical solenoid.
highlights.ANA2019: Structures of Rag GTPase heterodimers bound to mTORC1 reveal lysosomal recruitment mechanism.

Chi H.lab_name: St. Jude Children's Research Hospital, Department of Immunology
Chi H.role: Defines how mTORC1 signaling builds immune tolerance in regulatory T cells
Chi H.sub: PhD, University of Rochester · now Chair, Department of Immunology, St. Jude; Robert G. Webster Endowed Chair in Immunology
story: His 2012 review (CHI2012) became a foundational reference for immunometabolism. In 2013 (ZEN2013), with Hu Zeng, showed mTORC1 (via Raptor) is required for Tregs to integrate metabolic cues and mature into suppressive cells — overturning the assumption Tregs are simply low-mTOR cells.

Chairs St. Jude Immunology, co-directs the Center of Excellence for Pediatric Immuno-Oncology. NCI Outstanding Investigator Award (2021), AAAS Fellow (2023), ICIS-BioLegend William E. Paul Award (2025), elected to National Academy of Sciences (2026).

highlights.CHI2012: Foundational review synthesizing how mTOR governs T-cell fate decisions.
highlights.ZEN2013: mTORC1 (via Raptor) required for Tregs to integrate metabolic signals and establish suppressive function.

Abraham RT.role: Co-discovered mTOR and showed it directly controls protein synthesis
Abraham RT.sub: Mayo Clinic · Duke University Medical Center · Burnham Institute · Pfizer Oncology Research · Vividion Therapeutics · now Engine Biosciences (per most recent record, May 2026)
story: At Mayo Clinic, isolated mTOR ('RAFT1') using a rapamycin-FKBP12 bait (SAB1995) — one of three independent 1994–95 papers (alongside Schreiber's and Sabatini/Snyder's) founding the field. In 1997 (BRU1997), showed mTOR directly phosphorylates PHAS-I (4E-BP1) — the paper behind nearly every mTOR→translation diagram.

Moved through Duke, Burnham Institute (TOR/ATM-ATR/T-cell signaling), Pfizer Oncology (San Diego), Vividion Therapeutics, now Engine Biosciences — over 30 years still working at the chemical-biology/cancer-drug-discovery interface.

highlights.SAB1995: Isolated mTOR ('RAFT1') via a rapamycin-FKBP12 affinity matrix — one of three independent founding papers.
highlights.BRU1997: Showed mTOR directly phosphorylates PHAS-I (4E-BP1), the mechanistic link to protein synthesis control.

Maier T.lab_name: Maier Lab, Biozentrum, University of Basel
Maier T.role: Solved the first cryo-EM structures of human mTORC1 and mTORC2
Maier T.sub: PhD, Freie Universität Berlin (Wolfram Saenger) · postdoc, ETH Zurich (Nenad Ban) · assistant professor, Biozentrum (2011) → associate (2016) → full professor of Structural Biology (2023)
story: Produced one of the first near-atomic structures of complete human mTORC1 (AYL2015), revealing its rigid dimeric assembly. Five years later, solved mTORC2 at 3.2 Å (SCA2020), pinpointing Rictor's C-terminal tail as the reason mTORC2 isn't directly blocked by rapamycin.
Trained under crystallographer Saenger, then cryo-EM pioneer Nenad Ban. Continues combining cryo-EM, X-ray, and computation to map large regulatory complexes at atomic resolution.

highlights.AYL2015: One of the first cryo-EM structures of complete human mTORC1, revealing dimeric architecture and active-site access.
highlights.SCA2020: Cryo-EM structure of human mTORC2 pinpoints Rictor's C-terminus as source of rapamycin insensitivity.

Ben-Sahra I.lab_name: Ben-Sahra Lab, Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine
Ben-Sahra I.role: Discovered that mTORC1 drives both halves of nucleotide synthesis, pyrimidines and purines, through two distinct mechanisms
Ben-Sahra I.sub: PhD, Université Côte d'Azur, France (Frédéric Bost lab, 2010) · postdoc, Harvard T.H. Chan School (Brendan D. Manning lab) · now Associate Professor, Northwestern Feinberg (since 2023)
story: As Manning-lab postdoc, showed (BEN2013) mTORC1–S6K1 switches on de novo pyrimidine synthesis by phosphorylating CAD. Three years later (BEN2016), showed mTORC1 also drives purine synthesis via ATF4-dependent activation of the mitochondrial tetrahydrofolate cycle — completing the picture that mTORC1 controls both nucleotide families.
Trained in Nice, France before Harvard postdoc; now runs his own lab at Northwestern's Lurie Comprehensive Cancer Center studying how growth signaling rewires metabolism in cancer and aging.

highlights.BEN2013: mTORC1–S6K1 switches on de novo pyrimidine synthesis by phosphorylating CAD.
highlights.BEN2016: mTORC1 drives purine synthesis via ATF4-dependent activation of the mitochondrial tetrahydrofolate cycle.
